messages:
sam: Heads-up — seeing intermittent packet fizzles hitting gpu backfill pods in us-west2-b for ~2h. Retransmit rate spikes up to 0.6% for short bursts, grpc clients log timeouts.
anya: Is this overlay or host networking? any RDMA in these jobs?
sam: Overlay CNI (geneve). No RDMA. Pods are host-tcp.
cheng: Pulled a tcpdump/sflow from gpu-node-63 — lots of segmented frames and occasional drops around jumbo boundary. Looks like some hosts are at 1500 MTU while others at 9000.
elena: We rolled a NIC/driver package to 5.12.14 on that AZ two days ago; possibly lost the MTU config on some images.
anya: Can you paste `ip link` + `ethtool -k` from an affected host?
sam: Paste from gpu-node-63:
```
Kernel: 5.12.14-rt
ip link show eth0: mtu 1500 qlen 1000
ethtool -k eth0:
  gro: on
  gso: on
  tso: on
```
cheng: If eth0 is 1500 but overlay expects 9000, you'll see fragmentation of geneve frames and some switches or NIC offloads may drop fragments. That matches the bursty retransmits.
elena: Confirmed: only the image batch for us-west2-b reverted MTU. Other AZs remained at 9000.
oncall-jordan: Mitigation idea: disable GRO/GSO/TCO on affected hosts to stop large segmented frames from confusing the overlay, then fix MTU persistently during maintenance.
sam: Quick mitigation I ran on one node — immediate improvement:
```
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 9000
```
cheng: Warning — don't change MTU before validating underlay path between TORs or you risk blackholing traffic. Verify switch MTU via fabric-api first.
anya: I checked fabric-api: us-west2-b TORs and aggregation have 9216 MTU enabled. Underlay is fine.
elena: Plan: 1) Run a scripted `ethtool -K` to disable offloads on the 12 affected GPU hosts as immediate mitigation. 2) During tonight window, persist MTU to 9000 in the image and restart networking. 3) If instability persists, rollback the driver to previous known-good.
oncall-jordan: I'm executing the gro/gso/tso disable now and tagging ops-bot to suppress noisy alerts.
ops-bot: Incident quieted for cluster=us-west2-b, reason="mitigation in progress: disabling NIC offloads on affected hosts" :white_check_mark:
sam: After disabling offloads on 6 hosts retransmits fell from ~0.5% -> 0.02% and grpc retries dropped. Backfills resumed.
cheng: Good signal. Still want end-to-end tests: `iperf3` (udp and tcp), `tcpdump -s0 -w` sampling around heavy traffic, and `ss -s` to check retrans counts.
anya: Also adding a fleet-image linter check to ensure MTU settings persist across kernel/driver updates. Ticket incoming.
elena: I'll open a driver-regression ticket and schedule rollback tests if we see any negative side-effects from offload toggles.
sam: +30m — monitoring stable, no new client timeouts. Leaving mitigations in place until maintenance. Will post a short blameless postmortem once we fix image pipeline.
cheng: For the postmortem, capture: image build step that writes /etc/network/interfaces, kernel package change, and a validation test that runs `ip link` after first boot.
oncall-jordan: Noted. I'll coordinate the maintenance window and include a smoke-checklist.
elena: Thanks all — keeping this thread open until the MTU is fixed fleet-wide.
sam: Update 2412347450 — maintenance scheduled 03:00 UTC, will flip MTU and re-enable offloads if stable.
